premises.text: Video post-production feedback today is fragmented across email, calendars, calls, and spreadsheets
premises.evidence_span: teams are running around, sifting through emails with long threads where someone hits reply all, scheduling meetings on calendars, long phone calls with people in multiple time zones

premises.text: A viewing room focuses stakeholders on the video so they can leave timestamped comments while watching
premises.evidence_span: the viewing room is the sole focus is on the video itself and to give feedback on it

premises.text: Quick-comment hotkeys speed repeated feedback while watching
premises.evidence_span: allowing users to set their own kind of quick comments

premises.text: A review-and-export pane digests stakeholder feedback and assigns edits to editors
premises.evidence_span: digest of all your stakeholders giving feedback

premises.text: Assigned markers export directly into editors' NLEs such as Adobe Premiere
premises.evidence_span: export it directly into his favorite video editing software

premises.text: Browser-based design uses existing hosting so IT has little to deploy
premises.evidence_span: browser-based, and we leverage existing hosting infrastructure

premises.text: Project-based pricing is affordable for small teams while scaling for larger clients
premises.evidence_span: project based pricing that's friendly to teams of all sizes

premises.text: Native Adobe integration and upcoming MPAA compliance target studio standards
premises.evidence_span: announcing our native integration with Adobe

value.text: Video professionals collaborate and manage post-production feedback without email chaos
value.evidence_span: communication and project management tool for video professionals

causal_links.evidence_span: collection is one part. You've got to make it actionable in some way
made it very, very easy to collect timestamp feedback
our markers actually show up directly in the timeline
IT departments specifically love us because it's browser-based
make it affordable for small teams while keep on producing upsides for larger clients

notes: Auto-pause/resume and reply-in-thread folded into P2 as cascade of the viewing-room feedback mechanism. Network-effect pilot counts excluded as traction. Adobe native integration kept with NLE export domain; MPAA compliance folded into P8 as institutional detail of the studio stack. Singletons D3 and D4 retained as separately revisable IT and pricing modules.
